tier2: rating >= 4 and no build red flag (weak-archetype flag excluded, see archetype_flag)

review.verdict: A low-curve WB go-wide deck with strong removal (3 Eaten Alive fed by Infestation Sage and cat tokens, Bake into a Pie, Nighthawk) and good synergy; it is light on late-game power, and Blasphemous Edict is a clunky fit for a creature-heavy plan.

Deep black removal suite (Downfall, Bake, Banishing Light, Eaten Alive, Banshee) plus two Nighthawks and two Elendas on a clean sac/drain curve; strong deck, only the odd off-color gain lands slightly weaken the mana.

A low, aggressive BR deck. It has plenty of cheap removal (Burst Lightning, Abrade, Eaten Alive, Stab, Immolators) and strong payoffs in Krenko and Perforating Artist. Its few 1/1 bodies and light top-end could run out of gas, and it might want 16 lands.

Six solid removal spells plus Vampire Nighthawk, Arbiter of Woe and Guarded Heir on a clean two-color curve. Fleeting Flight, Fake Your Own Death and Goldvein Pick are filler, and a few creatures are thin, but this is a strong, well-built deck.

Strong WB lifegain shell: four Dazzling Angels, five hard removal spells and Elenda on a good 2-3-4 curve. The mana is off, though: 9 white and 9 black sources for a mostly white deck, with off-color gain lands used as filler, and Pilfer is a weak slot.

Ten fliers boosted by three Empyrean Eagles and Kykar, backed by real interaction (Banishing Light, two Uncharted Voyage, Witness Protection, two Bigfin Bouncer). A focused, aggressive tempo deck; held back by low-impact filler (Goldvein Pick, Think Twice, Fleeting Distraction, Run Away Together) and no late-game threats, and with a curve that tops out at 4 it could cut to 16 lands.

Solid WG creature deck with strong white commons (3x Dazzling Angel, Serra Angel, Vanguard Seraph, 2x Prideful Parent), good removal in Banishing Light, 2x Luminous Rebuke and Bite Down, plus Anthem and Leyline Axe to push damage; a good curve and clean two-color mana, only slightly thin on cheap interaction.

A focused WR aggro deck with eight two-drops and premium removal (4 Luminous Rebuke, Banishing Light, 2 Heartfire Immolator); Rebuke is cheap once attackers force blocks or taps, and the go-wide payoffs (Claws Out, Armasaur Guide, Felidar Savior) back the plan.
A low, focused WG beatdown curve with three Banishing Light, two fight/bite spells, and Anthem plus Overrun as finishers; some filler like Librarian and the many x/1s keeps it short of exceptional.

Strong, well-curved WG deck. Two Arahbo, Serra Angel, Good-Fortune Unicorn and the token makers give a real cats/counters engine, and two Banishing Light plus four fight/bite spells handle threats. The only knocks are removal that depends on board presence and little reach in the air.

A synergistic go-wide WG build: Arahbo, Prideful Parents, Unicorns and Felidar Savior make a wide board, and Overrun turns it into a finisher. The low curve fits 16 lands plus Elves, but removal is light (two Banishing Light plus fights) and a few slots like Fleeting Flight and Healer's Hawk are filler.

A solid aggressive WR deck. Arahbo leads a real cat subtheme and the low curve backs it up. Two Abrade, Banishing Light and Heartfire Immolator give it good removal. Serra Angel, Dragon Trainer, Guarded Heir and Chandra give it a strong top end. Its only real weaknesses are the two Fleeting Flight and a slightly heavy 6+ slot for an aggro deck.
Tight RG power-matters deck with a low curve, 18 bodies, many power-4 enablers and strong fight/burn removal plus Drakuseth as a bomb finisher; a bit light on late game and card flow but very solid.

A low curve backed by plenty of cheap removal (Burst Lightning x2, Bite Down x2, Abrade, Fiery Annihilation) and strong top-end in Greatwurm and Sire makes this a solid, well-built RG deck. Only a thin middle and some filler bodies keep it from being great.

Strong, well-curved RG beatdown with premium uncommons (Krenko, Ashroot x2, Ruby x2, Vivien, Phoenix) and solid removal; the ferocious payoffs lean on only about six power-4 creatures, and Goldvein Picks are filler, but this is a clearly good deck.

Solid RG beatdown with a low curve, good removal (Burst Lightning, Fiery Annihilation, Bite Down, Felling Blow, Immolator), Overrun and Garruk's Uprising payoffs, and Sire as a bomb top end; a well-built, consistent deck.

Clean UG midrange: 19 creatures with good power on a smooth curve, plenty of fight and bounce removal (Bite Down x2, Felling Blow, Indrik x2, Bouncer x2, Voyage), Zimone as a strong payoff and solid mana; it lacks a true bomb and has little air defense beyond one Snarespinner.

Strong BR deck: deep, cheap removal (Burst Lightning x2, Abrade, Stab, Hero's Downfall, Incinerating Blast, plus three Heartfire Immolators) backs a real top end of three Dragon Trainers and the Drakuseth bomb. The main weak spots are a thin 3-drop slot, a slightly weak filler 1-2 drop (Burglar Rat, Fake Your Own Death), and the colorless Soulstone Sanctuary straining BB and RRR costs.

Solid UG deck: efficient 4-power green bodies power four fight and bite spells. Bigfin Bouncer, Uncharted Voyage and Witness Protection add interaction, and Curator and Sire give it a strong top end. Two counterspells and Fleeting Distraction are the soft spots.

Strong BR deck with a bomb in Liliana, plenty of efficient removal (2 Hero's Downfall, Burst Lightning, Eaten Alive, Immolators, Tragic Banshee) and a good curve. Three Brazen Scourge and High-Society Hunter give it real pressure. It loses some points for low-impact filler (Frenzied Goblin, Axgard Cavalry, Pilfer, Macabre Waltz) and for mana costs that are heavy in both colors on 8/7 lands.

Strong BG midrange with premium removal (2x Bake into a Pie, Hero's Downfall, Eaten Alive, Bite Down), Vivien Reid and a solid low curve of efficient green beaters; slightly light on late-game power but well built.

Strong BR raid deck with lots of removal (Heartfire x3, Downfall, Eaten Alive, Burst, Gorehorn x2) and good top end in Dragon Trainers and Arbiter; the green splash for only Bite Down and the near-blank Hidetsugu's Second Rite are needless slots, so cut both for BR playables and run a straight two-color base.

decks.playmat_name: ★★ good_22 · BG+u midrange ramp splash U · review 4/5

review.verdict: A strong BG removal-and-deathtouch midrange shell: Nighthawks, Downfall, Bake, Bite Down, Snarespinners, Lathril and Meteor Golem. Grow from the Ashes plus 5 fixing lands make the Tatyova and Koma splash workable, but Koma's UU will sometimes rot in hand.

A coherent WB sacrifice deck: Infestation Sage, Infernal Vessel, Gourmand and Arbiter of Woe feed each other, Elenda and Exemplar give it a real top end, and five pieces of removal back it up, but the 2-drops are small and Pilfer and Hungry Ghoul are filler.

Strong WB lifegain shell with a deep 2-3 drop curve, many token makers, premium removal (2 Bake, Banishing Light, 2 Rebuke, Eaten Alive) and Rune-Scarred Demon on top. Only Ravenous Amulet is weak; mana and curve are clean.

A solid WG counters deck: Ajani, Good-Fortune Unicorn, Inspiring Paladin and Wildwood Scourge pay off a real counter theme, and Banishing Light, two Luminous Rebuke and the fight spells give it plenty of interaction; mana and curve are clean, though Giada is just a 2/2 flier here and the six-drop Indriks make the top end a bit clunky.

Lean, aggressive RG deck with excellent removal (3 Burst Lightning, 2 Fiery Annihilation, fight spells) and a Drakuseth bomb. It is held back slightly because its payoffs (Hornbeetle, Ruby, Courageous Goblin) rely on only about six 4-power creatures.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_27 · RG+w power-4 aggro, light W splash · review 4/5

review.archetype: RG power-4 aggro, light W splash
review.verdict: Solid Gruul deck. It has real removal (Fiery Annihilation, Burst Lightning, two Bushwhack, Heartfire Immolator, plus splashed Banishing Light), top-end threats in Etali, Vivien and two Dragon Trainers, and a cheap splash on 4 white sources. It is held back slightly by filler like Reclamation Sage, Goldvein Pick and Thrill, and by a modest 14 bodies for the power-4 payoffs.

A focused, nearly mono-green elves deck. It has strong lords (Archdruid, Dwynen), Lathril, a Liliana bomb, Greatwurm and Overrun as finishers, and plenty of fight-based removal. The light black is backed by 6 sources plus mana elves. Its main weakness is that all the removal depends on having a board.

A coherent low-curve WU lifegain deck. Cat Collector x3, Hawks, Pridemate, Dazzling Angel and Felidar Savior work together well, but it has little hard removal, several filler tricks and no real finishers.

A solid, coherent BR raid/sacrifice deck with real removal (Bake into a Pie x2, Eaten Alive x2, Burst Lightning) and strong payoffs in Perforating Artist, High-Society Hunter and Arbiter of Woe, but many low-impact 2/2s for two cap its power at a fine deck rather than a great one.

A low-curve UB sacrifice deck: Infernal Vessel, Infestation Sage, Fake Your Own Death and Gourmand/Eaten Alive fit together, Dreadwing Scavengers and Downfall/Banshee/Bouncer give real quality, but filler 1-drops like Diregraf Ghoul and a thin late game cap it at a solid, unspectacular deck.

A solid white cat shell: Arahbo, three Prideful Parent, Cat Collector, Felidar Savior and Claws Out, plus Banishing Light and two Luminous Rebuke. The blue half is thin, with two Think Twice as filler, and Blossoming Sands and Thornwood Falls are off-color taplands that each make only one useful color, so it is a fine deck rather than a strong one.

A focused, well-curved RG power-4 aggro deck. Ramp from Elves and Ruby feeds strong cards like Ashroot Animist and Sylvan Scavenging, but it has only about four real removal spells, almost no late game or card advantage, and filler like Courageous Goblin and two Giant Growths, so it is solid but not exceptional.

A playable low-curve WB deck with real payoffs in Nighthawk, Blight-Priest, Arena, Angel and Guarded Heir, but many weak 1-drops and only two Bake into a Pie for spot removal; Day of Judgment fights its own go-wide plan, and Pilfer and Waltz are filler.

Coherent UR spells deck with good payoffs in Balmor x2, the prowess creatures, Kiora and Curator, and Micromancer finds Burst Lightning, but real removal is thin (2 Burst, Immolator, a bounce). Think Twice x2 and two Refutes make it reactive and durdly, and the deck is heavily blue on a 9/8 land split, so it plays fine but not great.

A low-curve WR go-wide deck with real Cat synergy (Arahbo, 3x Prideful Parent) and good burn, but filler like Axgard Cavalry and Courageous Goblin plus almost no top end make it a fine deck rather than a strong one; 17 lands is one too many for this curve.
A playable WB value deck with good recursion and decent fliers, but it has only two clean removal spells, Blasphemous Edict clashes with its go-wide board, and the double Seeker's Folly is filler.

Solid WB deck with good removal (Downfall, Eaten Alive, Rebuke, Stab, Banshee), strong top end in Arbiter and High-Society Hunter, and a light lifegain package. White has twice as many cards as black, so 8/8 basics should lean toward Plains, and filler like Fleeting Flight and the Hawks keeps it from being more than fine.

Liliana, Serra Angel and a decent removal suite lift a deck padded with low-impact bodies (Burglar Rats, Hart, Banner, Fake Your Own Death), and Day of Judgment works against its own creature plan; fine but not strong.

Solid UB shell with three Bake into a Pie, Bloodthirsty Conqueror and good flyers, but only 13 creatures and filler like Macabre Waltz, Think Twice and Run Away Together dilute it; two Tolarian Terrors are fine with about 10 instants and sorceries.

Solid removal suite and decent fliers with Eagle and Terrors, but Think Twice, double Refute, and a Wrath in a creature tempo deck pull it between plans and dilute card quality; a fine but unexceptional deck.

Solid blue-white shell with good top end (Curator, Exemplar, Icewind, Tolarian Terror fed by about 9 instants) and decent interaction, but the walls, cantrip filler and thin lifegain payoffs leave it short on pressure. It's a fine deck, not a strong one.

Strong burn and tempo (3 Burst Lightning, Fiery Annihilation, Bigfin bounce) plus a Chandra bomb and Sphinx, but the thin, small creature base struggles to pressure or hold the board, and Slagstorm hits its own 2/1s.

Lean, well-built RG aggro deck: low curve, 15 lands are fine with four mana creatures, and plenty of cheap fight/burn removal. But only about six creatures turn on the power-4 payoffs (Ruby, Hornbeetle, Goblin), and there are no bombs and little card advantage to win long games.

Five mana dorks plus two Loot ramp into strong top end: Etali, Ghalta, Dragon Trainer, Needletooth and two Gorehorn Raiders. Only Abrade, Bushwhack and Heartfire are real removal, and the many 1/1 dorks are weak on their own, so the deck is solid but not exceptional.

Solid UW deck with good removal (2 Banishing Light, Rebuke, Make Your Move, Witness Protection, Voyage), a strong top end in Curator and Guarded Heir, and clean mana. The 2-drops are low-impact (3 Elementalist Adept), and there aren't enough fliers to make full use of Empyrean Eagle.

A real UR spells shell with Balmor x2, three Whelps, Archmage and a Drakuseth bomb, but three Think Twice, Time Stop, Aegis Turtle and a pile of counterspells leave it short on threats and burn, so it plays too reactively to be more than fine.
Clean, well-curved white-heavy flier deck with strong commons (3 Dazzling Angel, 2 Empyrean Eagle, Guarded Heir), but only Uncharted Voyage as removal leaves it racing bombs it cannot answer.
Strong top end and interaction (2 Curator, 2 Banishing Light, 2 Bigfin, Trickster, Aetherize), but walls, Think Twice, Goldvein Pick and Self-Reflection make it short on real threats to close games.

A coherent, low-curve WG creature deck: two Anthems over 17 bodies plus Beast-Kin Rangers, Dazzling Angels and Unicorn give it real pressure, but with only three removal spells, almost nothing above 4 mana and 17 lands for a curve topping at 5, it is a solid but unspectacular aggro deck.

Solid UB shell with good top end (Arbiter of Woe, Dreadwing Scavengers, Skyship Buccaneer) and decent sac fodder, but only about three real removal spells, several weak 1/1s, and just six instants/sorceries, so the Tolarian Terrors often cost too much. Playable, middling deck.

A coherent, well-curved RW aggro deck with good top end (Serra, Guarded Heir, Sire, Gorehorn) and go-wide finishers, but it has very little removal and some filler 2-drops (Axgard Cavalry x2, Frenzied Goblin).

Solid BR raid shell with real removal (2 Eaten Alive, Fiery Annihilation, 2 Tragic Banshee) and strong gold cards (Perforating Artist x2, Alesha); held back by many weak 1/1s and discard filler like Pilfer, Tinybones and Axgard Cavalry. A fine deck, not a great one.

Low-curve red aggro with blue tempo and a solid 2-drop base. Removal is thin beyond Burst Lightning, Abrade and Imprisoned, and several filler cards (Thrill, Bulk Up, Cerberus) make it a fine but unspectacular deck; Etali is a strong top end.

A low-curve red aggro deck with real removal (4 Heartfire Immolator, Fiery Annihilation, Stab, Firebrands), but black is only five mediocre cards on 7 Swamps against heavy red needs, and it runs out of power after turn 4.

Solid WU tempo deck with a good curve, three Skyship Buccaneers, Kaito and a removal suite of Banishing Light, Bigfin Bouncer and Uncharted Voyage. Several weak 2-drops (Skyknight Squire, Brineborn Cutthroat, Think Twice) and few real bombs make it a fine deck, not a great one.

Solid UB value deck with real bombs and finishers (High-Society Hunter, Rune-Scarred Demon, Tragic Banshee) and good removal (Bake into a Pie, Eaten Alive, Meteor Golem), but the low end is padded with weak cards like Hungry Ghoul, Fleeting Distraction, Think Twice and reactive counters, which caps its power.

Coherent WU flier tempo deck with a smooth curve, strong uncommons (Dazzling Angel, Exemplar, Empyrean Eagle, Giada) and good instant-speed tricks, but removal is thin beyond two Luminous Rebuke and Witness Protection, and Goldvein Pick and Scrawling Crawler are filler.

Solid BG deck with real removal (Downfall, Pie, two fight spells, two Banshees) and death synergies via Skeleton, Sage, Spinner and Needletooth, but Pilfer, Seeker's Folly and Burglar Rat are weak, and Quakestrider's GGG on 8 Forests is clunky.

Coherent RG ferocious curve with good synergy (Garruk's Uprising, Goblins, Ruby, Hornbeetle) and solid mana, but light removal and three defensive Snarespinners dilute the aggro plan; a fine, unexceptional deck.

Solid RW aggro deck with real removal (2 Fiery Annihilation, Banishing Light, Rebuke, Immolator, Gorehorn pings) and Shivan Dragon on top. Raid synergy and a good curve, but the filler is mediocre (Axgard Cavalry, Goldvein Pick, Healer's Hawk) and it has few strong rares, so it's a fine deck rather than a great one.

A coherent WG go-wide deck: three Hare Apparent, Beast-Kin Rangers and Overrun as the finisher, on a low curve that suits 16 lands. Removal is thin (Banishing Light, Bite Down, Joust Through), and Divine Resilience, Snakeskin Veil and two Librarians are filler, so it's a fine deck but not a strong one.

A solid WG deck with a clean curve and six real removal spells, mostly fight effects backed by sturdy bodies. It has light lifegain synergy through Cat Collector, Dazzling Angel and Felidar Savior, but no bombs and a thin top end beyond Herald, so it is fine rather than strong.

Real payoffs carry a playable BR sacrifice deck: two Arbiter of Woe, Etali, Gorehorn Raiders and Tragic Banshee, with sticky fodder (Infernal Vessel, Infestation Sage). But it has one 3-drop and six cards at 5+, plus filler like Pilfer, Thrill and three Hungry Ghoul, and only Burst Lightning and Stab as cheap interaction, so it's fine but not great.

Solid RW aggro with deep, cheap removal (Burst x2, Abrade, Banishing Light, Rebuke, Incinerating Blast) and good tops in Krenko, Dragon Trainer and Gorehorn Raider. Filler like Axgard Cavalry, Fanatical Firebrand and Goldvein Pick, plus only two 3-drops, keeps it a fine deck rather than a great one.

A low-curve UR spells deck: Abrade x3, Fiery Annihilation, Heartfire Immolator x3 and Firebrands give real removal and Balmor pays off spells, but the bodies are small and the only big threats are Dragon Trainer and Etali, so it can run out of pressure in long games.
A coherent BR sacrifice deck with lots of cheap removal and threaten-plus-sac synergy, but its bodies are small and fragile, it has only two 3-drops, and 17 lands is a lot for this low curve.

A coherent low-curve BR raid and sacrifice deck. Perforating Artist, Alesha and cheap removal carry it, but the four Infestation Sages and filler like Axgard Cavalry, Tinybones and Thrill leave it light on power and late-game threats. The black-heavy cards also want more Swamps than an even 8/8 split, and with this curve 16 lands would be enough.

A solid, low-curve GW creature deck: four Beast-Kin Rangers, token makers and two Preposterous Proportions give it a real go-wide finish. But Bushwhack is the only removal, Grow from the Ashes is filler, and the Elf and Cat synergies are each too thin to pay off reliably.

Solid WR deck. Drakuseth, two Dragon Trainers, Dazzling Angels and three Banishing Lights give it real power, but the cheap Hawks and Hunters are filler bodies, it has only four true removal spells, and Drakuseth's RRR is tight on 8 red sources.

A clean, low-curve WR tokens/aggro deck with good cheap removal (Burst Lightning, 2 Abrade, Banishing Light, Immolator) and fine mana, but it has no real payoff or bomb, so it relies on filler-quality bodies and could stall against bigger boards.
Solid blue tempo shell with flying pressure, bounce, two Fiery Annihilations and an Embercleave payoff; it is held back by thin red removal, two clunky Refutes and an RR bomb on only 8 red sources.

A coherent, low-curve green aggro deck with a light white splash, 14 two-drops and Vivien Reid on top. Removal is thin (only Bite Down, plus Vivien's -3 against fliers), and many bodies are filler 2/2s and 3/1s, so it can stall against bigger boards or lose to evasion; it could also run 16 lands.

A coherent, low-curve WR aggro deck with real burn and enough bodies. Many filler 1-2 drops (Firebrands, Courageous Goblin) and little lifegain for Cat Collector or cats for Claws Out keep it a solid deck rather than a strong one.

Solid UG ramp shell built around a Koma bomb, with good interaction (Bigfin, 2 Voyage, Imprisoned, Indrik, Bushwhack) and real ramp. A few filler slots (Aegis Turtle, Hornbeetle) and little defense against fliers keep it a fine deck rather than a great one.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_76 · WR go-wide aggro with lifegain/cats · review 3/5

review.verdict: Solid WR aggro with good removal (3 Banishing Light, Burst Lightning, Rebuke, Raider) and a real Cat Collector/Healer's Hawk lifegain engine. Weak filler like Frenzied Goblin, Axgard Cavalry, Katana and Fleeting Flight, plus few bodies that hold up late, keep it a fine deck rather than a great one.

A coherent UR spells deck. Krenko, Archmage of Runes, Balmor, Tolarian Terror and Skyship Buccaneer give it real power, and three Burst Lightning plus instant-speed tokens fit the plan. Removal is thin beyond Burst and Heartfire, the 2-drops are fragile, and the two Sure Strikes are filler, so it is fine but not exceptional.

A solid green core: Beast-Kin Rangers, Cackling Prowlers, Snarespinners, Spinner, Sylvan Scavenging and Stomper give a sound curve and good bodies. The blue half is thin: Think Twice, Mystic and Refute do little, and removal is only Bite Down plus two clunky Voyages. Green is the main color, so 9/9 lands should be about 10 Forest / 8 Island. A fine but unexciting deck.

A real UR spells deck with strong payoffs (3 Balmor, 3 Tolarian Terror) and a good curve, but only 8 instants feed them, the cantrips are low-impact, and hard removal is thin (Burst Lightning, Gorehorn, bounce), so it can stall against bigger boards.

Solid BG midrange with plenty of cheap interaction (3 Stab, 2 Hero's Downfall, Bite Down, Banshees) and a reasonable 15-creature curve. It lacks bombs and card advantage, Blasphemous Edict is a clunky 5-mana wipe in a creature deck, and the Librarians are low-impact.

A solid Izzet spells deck built on Archmage of Runes, Niv-Mizzet, Balmor and Micromancer fetching Burst Lightning. Removal past the three burn spells is thin, the six-plus slot is clunky, and Cerberus plus the cantrips are filler, so it lands as a fine 3.

Playable BG midrange with a decent creature base. Removal is light (Stab, Bake into a Pie, Indrik fight), and filler like Goldvein Pick, Pilfer and two Zombifys with few big targets or self-mill makes it merely fine.

Solid UG deck with strong blue top end (Curator, two High Fae Tricksters, Buccaneer, Icewind), good fight spells and a fine curve. Removal is light, the elf package is too small to pay off, and only 7 Forests support a green-heavy 2-drop slot.

A solid UG ramp shell. Llanowar Elves and ramp lead into Koma and Quilled Greatwurm, and Micromancer fetches Bushwhack or Veil. But the green-heavy cards, with GG costs and green one-drops, want more than 8 Forests, and fight-based removal is thin with mostly small bodies.
A coherent UR spells deck with good cheap burn, Fiery Annihilation and Tolarian Terror, but four counterspells and a thin, fragile creature base leave it short on threats to close games.

A solid BG deck with plenty of cheap removal (3 Stab, 2 Bite Down, Eaten Alive, Bushwhack, Banshee), good 4-power bodies for fight spells, and strong top end in High-Society Hunter and Arbiter of Woe. The light sacrifice package and several 1/1 filler creatures keep it from being more than fine.
Solid BG creature curve with good value (Wardens, Lathril, Vivien, Overrun, recursion), but only Stab and Vivien's -3 as removal leaves it weak to opposing bombs and fliers.

Solid BG creature-recursion shell with real top end (Nighthawk, Arbiter, Soulcallers, Needletooth), but only two true removal spells, and Pilfer, Seeker's Folly and Burglar Rat spend slots on low-impact discard.

A coherent BG sacrifice deck with good removal (2 Bake into a Pie, Eaten Alive, 2 Stab, 2 Indrik fights) and real sacrifice synergy (Sage, Vessel, Nine-Lives, Gourmand, Wardens, Arbiter), but many 1/1s and three 6-drops make the board a bit weak; a fine, playable deck.

Solid UG deck with plenty of fight-based removal (2 Bushwhack, Bite Down, Indrik) plus Witness Protection and Uncharted Voyage, and good green bodies to fight with. Splashing white just for Celestial Armor isn't worth it. A light creature count and filler like Heraldic Banner and Scrawling Crawler keep it at average; cut the splash for another creature.

Solid UB with real synergy (Micromancer fetching Stab or Witness Protection, Infernal Vessel feeding Arbiter of Woe, Bake into a Pie and Bigfin Bouncer as removal), but two Refutes, Think Twice and Hungry Ghoul are filler and the deck lacks a bomb to close games.

Functional UG midrange: Zimone, the Sire, fight spells (Bite Down, Felling Blow, Bushwhack) and Uncharted Voyage give real interaction and a good curve. But filler like Aegis Turtle, double Think Twice and Goldvein Pick, plus a weak elf subtheme, keep it at average.

Solid UG deck. Three Bite Down, Bushwhack, Indrik, Bigfin Bouncer and Uncharted Voyage give real interaction, and Zimone plus two Skyship Buccaneers add quality. But several 1-2 power bodies make the fight and bite spells unreliable, and two Refutes are clunky filler, so it's a fine deck rather than a great one.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_94 · UG G stompy, light blue (Koma) · review 3/5

review.verdict: A solid green beatdown deck with good fight removal (Bite Down x2, Bushwhack, Indrik) and strong top end in Quilled Greatwurm and Koma, but the blue half is only Bouncers, Koma and a clunky Epiphany, and Librarian and Grow from the Ashes are filler, so it's a fine deck rather than a great one.

Strong black removal (3 Bake into a Pie, Hero's Downfall, Eaten Alive) plus blue card draw and tempo makes a solid UB control deck, but the red splash only buys Balmor, a gold 2-drop. Its 2 Mountains plus Cliffs leave just 8 blue sources, which strains the BB/UU costs. Cut the splash for an Island and a creature.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_96 · UB+w spells/control splash W · review 3/5

review.verdict: Solid UB tempo-control with good cheap removal (3 Stab, Downfall, Banshee) and Micromancer-Stab value, but only 9 instants and sorceries for two Tolarian Terrors, a thin early board, and a three-card white splash (Felidar Savior isn't worth splashing) make it a fine deck rather than a strong one.

Solid UB tempo-control shell with real power (3 Dreadwing Scavenger, Kaito, Archmage, 2 Tolarian Terror fed by about 10 instants and sorceries) and plenty of interaction including two wraths, but the body count is thin, Turtle and Campus Guide are filler, and splashing red on 3 sources for a single Fiery Annihilation adds little for the mana risk.
